classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate equal production across 13 vats, cylindrical can capacity and unit conversions, then distinguish whole cans from approximate can volumes.

inlines.text: Each day a factory produces 5000 litres of soft drink in their 13 vats.
The soft drink is distributed in cans 13 centimetres high with diameter 6.5 centimetres.
How many cans does one vat produce each day?

answer.short: 891 completely filled cans, or approximately 892 cans by volume, assuming equal production per vat.
answer.worked:
Assuming equal production across the 13 vats and cylindrical cans:
$$\begin{align*} r &= 6.5\div2\text{ cm} \\ r &= 3.25\text{ cm} \\ V_{\text{can}} &= \pi r^2h \\ V_{\text{can}} &= \pi(3.25)^2(13)\text{ cm}^3 \\ V_{\text{can}} &= \frac{2197\pi}{16}\text{ cm}^3 \\ C_{\text{can}} &= \frac{2197\pi}{16}\text{ mL} \\ C_{\text{vat}} &= \frac{5000\times1000}{13}\text{ mL} \\ C_{\text{vat}} &= \frac{5\,000\,000}{13}\text{ mL} \\ \text{Number of cans} &= \frac{5\,000\,000}{13}\div\frac{2197\pi}{16} \\ \text{Number of cans} &= \frac{80\,000\,000}{28\,561\pi} \\ \text{Number of cans} &\approx 891.59 \end{align*}$$
This fills 891 cans completely, or is approximately 892 cans by volume.
